name: Bodyweight Aesthetics
description:
5-day per week routine, using only your bodyweight, no equipment or gym needed. Each session lasts approximately 90 minutes. The goal is to achieve an aesthetic, proportional, and symmetrical physique.


Weekly structure:

• Push and Core - Metabolic: Training focused on pushes, triceps and abs, with little recovery and high intensity.

• Legs and Glutes - Relative Strength: Focus on lower body and glutes, high volume and unilateral emphasis for maximum stimulus without external load.

• Push and Core with Deltoid Emphasis: Focus on push for shoulders and triceps, combined with advanced core and metabolic intensity.

• Legs and Core - Maximum Density: Unilateral and bilateral variety in leg, glute and oblique abdomen. Emphasis on technique before speed.

• Push and Core - Powerful Finish: Advanced push and abs to close the week, high frequency and accumulated fatigue control.

Designed for intermediates who want to progress and improve their body composition.

name: Total Strength at Home
description:
4-day per week routine, using only your bodyweight, no equipment or gym needed. Each session lasts approximately 90 minutes. The goal is to build strength and develop muscle progressively.


Weekly structure:

• Push and Core - Hypertrophy: Push training (chest, triceps, anterior deltoids and core). A session that prioritizes range of motion and repetition quality.

• Legs and Glutes - Bodyweight Knockout: Dominant focus on legs and glute area, ensuring global recruitment and strategic muscle fatigue in lower limbs.

• Explosive Push and Abs: Advanced push and abs session, with eccentric loads and emphasis on explosive variants.

• Legs and Glutes Variant - Hypertrophy: Lower body dominant training. New stimulus of variants to ensure global growth and muscle balance.

Ideal for beginners looking to build a solid foundation of strength and technique.

name: Home Toning
description:
3-day per week routine, using only your bodyweight, no equipment or gym needed. Each session lasts approximately 90 minutes. The main goal is to develop and tone the lower body, with special attention to glutes, hamstrings, and quads.


Weekly structure:

• Full Body - Aesthetic Base: Full body training with key exercises for chest, legs, glutes and core. Control and quality in each repetition are fundamental.

• Full Body - Polish and Volume: Secondary emphasis on pushes and legs, focus on details for even hypertrophy and strong stabilizer core.

• Full Body - Athletic Finish: Focus on advanced full body techniques to finish the week with maximum muscle congestion, emphasis on core, glutes and shoulders.

Ideal for beginners looking to build a solid foundation of strength and technique.

name: Equipment-Free Transformation
description:
6-day per week routine, using only your bodyweight, no equipment or gym needed. Each session lasts approximately 90 minutes. The goal is to build muscle mass and volume through high-intensity training.


Weekly structure:

• Push Day - Chest, Triceps and Core: Push training focused on pectorals, triceps, anterior deltoids and abdominal work. Use of supersets for maximum congestion and metabolic work.

• Pull Day - Back, Biceps and Core: Pull and core day where towel row variants and bodyweight are used, emphasizing back, biceps and central stability work.

• Leg Day - Total Lower Body: Lower body training: quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings and calves through unilateral variants and posterior chain movements.

• Push & Core - Shoulders, Triceps and Abs: Second focus on pushes and abs. Same metabolic focus and rep density to stimulate hypertrophy and muscular endurance.

• Pull & Core Day - Back, Biceps and Abs: Pull, dorsal and core day, repeating patterns and variants for maximum weekly frequency.

• Total Lower Body - Legs and Glutes: Second round of lower body, repetitions and variants for hypertrophy and strength-endurance. High frequency for maximum adaptation.

Designed for intermediates who want to progress and improve their body composition.

exercises.name: Flat Bench Press (Barbell)
exercises.note: Start light and prioritize technique.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.note: Hinge forward with a neutral spine; pull to your stomach.

exercises.name: High Bar Squat
exercises.note: Start light and prioritize technique.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift DB
exercises.note: Hips back, neutral spine; feel the hamstring stretch.

exercises.name: Unilateral Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.note: Reps per leg, dumbbell on the same side.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.note: Control the rotation; both sides count as one rep.

exercises.name: One-Arm DB Row
exercises.note: Reps per arm, supported on the bench.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raises
exercises.note: Raise to shoulder height, no swinging.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Squat DB
exercises.note: Reps per leg, dumbbells at your sides.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.note: Upper back on the bench; squeeze your glutes at the top.

exercises.name: Lying Dumbbell Leg Curl
exercises.note: Dumbbell held between your feet, lying on the bench.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.note: Pause for 1 second at the top of each rep.

exercises.name: Alternating Bicep Curl (Dumbbell)
exercises.note: Reps per arm, alternating.

exercises.name: Walking Lunges
exercises.note: Half the reps per leg, long controlled steps.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.note: Squeeze your glutes for 1-2 seconds at the top.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.note: Hold for the indicated seconds with a tight core.
